newsitem.title: JAPAN: Russia budget holds up Japan platinum talks.
newsitem.headline: Russia budget holds up Japan platinum talks.

text.p: The Russian state platinum group has informed Japanese traders that their regular year-end negotiations on export contracts are being held up by a delay in approving the Russian state budget.

"At the present time, we are unable to discuss the prolongation of existing contracts of Platinum Group Metals (PGMs) for January 1997, as we used to do previously," according to a letter sent by Almazjuvelirexport to Japanese clients. A copy of the letter was obtained by Reuters.
"It is because the State Budget of the Russian Federation for the next year is not approved yet and export quotas are submitted to Almaz only on its basis," it said.
Japan is the world's largest consumer of platinum group metals.
The Russian platinum group export agency usually sends a delegation to Japan in mid-December to negotiate its annual export contracts for the coming year.

Japanese traders said they were still waiting for Almaz to tell them about the schedule for Japan-Russian platinum talks, adding that they expected the mission to Japan to be delayed until next January or February.
The letter expressed the hope that the agency would be able to advise clients on the timetable for talks in the "nearest future".
The Russian parliament rejected a draft budget in October and is due to discuss another draft shortly. -- Tokyo Commodity Desk (81-3-3432-7431)
